messages:
Sam Lee: incident-bot paged at 06:02 UTC — continuous-batch CPU and latency spike in us-east-1. KV cache resident size climbed 4x, evictions and downstream 504s. Seeing microbatch sizes balloon to ~128 for a subset of requests. Marking for oncall triage.
incident-bot: ALERT: continuous-batch: high-latency (p99 > 800ms) across 3 clusters — affected: prod-us-east-1a,b. Trigger=kv_cache_growth_rate.
Evan S: seeing same in metrics. KV cache keys/sec jumped ~300% starting 06:00. Heap on runtime nodes trending up. Could be prefetch loop + high concurrency.
Irene M: query logs show many small requests getting merged into huge microbatches, then KV cache prefetch triggered repeatedly — likely bad prefetch heuristic at high concurrency.
Sam Lee: immediate mitigation proposals: 1) reduce prefetch window from 1024->256, 2) cap microbatch size to 32, 3) enable kv-prefetch-throttle feature flag to 0.5. Which do we want live now?
Priya K: do 1+2 now. 3 is feature flag riskier (needs rollout), but we can toggle if 1+2 insufficient.
Evan S: agreed. I'll push hotpatch to orchestration to set BATCH_MAX_MICROBATCH=32 and PREFETCH_LOOKAHEAD=256 for prod-us-east-1. Rolling out to 10% canary first.
Sam Lee: assign oncall to Evan. Priya, can you coordinate customer-impact comms? We need who is affected (dedicated vs hosted) and estimate scale.
oncall: Pager duty assignment -> Evan S (oncall) at 06:05 UTC.
incident-bot: runbook snippet attached: 
```
# apply hotpatch
kubectl set env deployment/continuous-batch PREFETCH_LOOKAHEAD=256 BATCH_MAX_MICROBATCH=32 -n prod-us-east-1
# reduce prefetch aggressive scoring
curl -X POST https://orchestrator/api/flags -d '{"kv-prefetch-score-threshold": 0.75}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
```
Evan S: canary deploy started at 06:12 UTC -> 6 nodes (10%). Watching CPU, KV-resident, p99.
Irene M: telemetry after canary: p99 dropped from 820ms->260ms on canary nodes, KV resident dropped ~60% on those nodes. Good signal.
Sam Lee: roll to 50% now. Rolling config via rollout job, ETA ~4m.
Priya K: customer-impact quick note: host API saw increased 5xx and timeouts between 06:00-06:10. Top affected customers: two mid-market tenants on dedicated pools in us-east-1 (IDs redacted) — estimated 12% of production traffic. We should send interim note: "We observed elevated latencies and timeouts; mitigation in progress; follow-up with RCA and ETA."
Evan S: roll to 100% at 06:22 UTC. Post-roll metrics: cluster p99 = 220ms, error rate back to baseline. KV resident stabilized.
Sam Lee: ok begin postmortem capture: impact window 06:00-06:22 UTC. Root cause hypothesis: prefetch heuristic combined with high concurrency produced runaway prefetch and extremely large microbatches, causing KV cache blowup and backpressure -> queueing and p99 cliffs.
Irene M: collecting logs for sample request traces and KV prefetch traces. Dumping to /var/tmp/cb-traces/1745123456.tar.gz.
Priya K: drafted customer notification in #customer-status: "At ~06:00 UTC we experienced a service degradation impacting request latencies for some customers in us-east-1. We deployed a configuration hotfix at 06:12 UTC and completed rollout at 06:22 UTC. Most customers saw restored service within minutes; dedicated pools may have seen prolonged errors. Working on full RCA." Feedback? :eyes:
Sam Lee: LGTM. Add note to call out mitigation steps (prefetch window + microbatch cap) and planned follow-ups (backfill canary tests for prefetch heuristics under synthetic concurrency, add circuit breaker for prefetch growth, add alert for microbatch size anomaly).
Evan S: leaving handoff to Priya for next 8h. I'll update any follow-ups I find in the playbook doc.
Priya K: taking over oncall handoff at 06:35 UTC. I'll coordinate postmortem, timeline, and customer comms. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — incident state -> mitigated at 06:25 UTC.
Priya K: final notes for handoff doc: detection -> 06:02, mitigations applied -> 06:12 canary, 06:22 full rollout, resolved -> 06:25. Impact estimate included. Next action items: add microbatch size anomaly alert (SRE-456), add prefetch circuit breaker (ENG-789), add regression test for prefetch under >10k concurrent qps (QA-112).
Sam Lee: closing thread — if anything else crops up ping Priya.
